method to poll the operation result at intervals as recommended by the API

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the operation resource.

post.summary:
Waits until the specified long-running operation is done or reaches at most
a specified timeout, returning the latest state.  If the operation is
already done, the latest state is immediately returned.  If the timeout
specified is greater than the default HTTP/RPC timeout, the HTTP/RPC
timeout is used.  If the server does not support this method, it returns
`google.rpc.Code.UNIMPLEMENTED`.
Note that this method is on a best-effort basis.  It may return the latest
state before the specified timeout (including immediately), meaning even an
immediate response is no guarantee that the operation is done.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the operation resource to wait on.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description:
The maximum duration to wait before timing out. If left blank, the wait
will be at most the time permitted by the underlying HTTP/RPC protocol.
If RPC context deadline is also specified, the shorter one will be used.

post.summary:
TriggerTenantWorkflow triggers a tenant-level workflow (e.g., inventory) for the
caller's tenant, fanning out to all eligible providers. Internally invokes the
same composer that runs during scheduled triggers, scoped to the caller's tenant
(the schedule policy is forced to is_global=false for the synthetic schedule).
post.description:
The tenant is derived from the request context (acontext.IdentityContext.GetTenant).
Permissions follow the same RBAC pattern as the other RPCs on this service.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
TriggerTenantWorkflowRequest triggers a tenant-level workflow for the caller's
tenant by composing tasks via the registered or generic composer.

Behavior mirrors the global-schedule path in knot: a synthetic schedule is built
for the caller's tenant with is_global=false, then handed to the appropriate
composer (e.g., InventoryTenantComposer for INVENTORY workflows). The resulting
task definitions are persisted as a single tenant-level workflow with provider
child workflow tasks.

At least one of {workflow_definition_id, workflow_type} must be supplied:
  * workflow_definition_id alone   - load that exact definition; its Type drives
                                     the composer choice.
  * workflow_type alone            - server resolves the canonical
                                     WorkflowDefinition for the type. For types
                                     backed by a hard-coded composer (currently
                                     INVENTORY) the server falls back to default
                                     values when no row exists. For types that
                                     depend on the generic composer (ANALYTICS,
                                     SUGGESTED_OWNERS, QUERY_CACHE_TIME_DEPENDENT)
                                     a row MUST exist because the recipe lives
                                     in WorkflowDefinition.task_definitions.
  * both                           - workflow_definition_id wins; workflow_type
                                     is validated to match WD.Type.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
- INVENTORY_PARENT_WF: Parent workflow type that creates child INVENTORY workflows via ANDROMEDA_WORKFLOW tasks
This type bypasses per-provider blocking for INVENTORY workflows, preventing deadlocks
 - SUGGESTED_OWNERS: Workflow type for resolving suggested owners from TSDB logs
 - DELTASYNC_SYNC: Workflow type for delta sync sync phase (reads DELTA mode resources from IR, publishes to Kepler)
Mutually exclusive with INVENTORY workflows per provider
 - ANALYTICS: Workflow type for analytics runs (behavior models, and future analytics tasks like lsp-eps, Galileo).
Scheduled via knot; runs at GLOBAL level. Managed by AnalyticsController.
 - ON_DEMAND_ANALYSIS: Generic on-demand analysis workflow. Routes to any service implementing ExecutionService.
Use for per-tenant, API-triggered analyses (ariel group anomaly, unused groups, etc.).
Independent concurrency from ANALYTICS — does not block behavior model runs.
 - TEST_CONNECTIVITY: Workflow type for testing provider connectivity
 - GRAPH_SYNC: Workflow type for async graph sync operations in polaris (ToolApplication, AccessPolicy, PolicyBinding).
 - GRAPH_JANITOR: Workflow type for the monthly graph soft-delete janitor. Scheduled via knot;
runs at GLOBAL level as a single Kubernetes Job (GRAPH_JANITOR task, KUBERNETES runtime).

parameters.name: includeSensitive
parameters.description:
When true, sensitive fields (currently the OAuth client_secret) are
populated on the response instead of being masked by the shared
provider-config Get handler. Default false preserves the
always-redacted behavior callers see today. Callers must hold a
role permitted by this service's read_roles (currently
ADMIN_READ_ONLY); audit logs should treat any request with this
flag set as a sensitive read.

parameters.name: decryptSensitive
parameters.description:
When true (and include_sensitive is also true), the secret is
decrypted server-side via the secrets manager before being
returned. When false, the encrypted ciphertext / secret-manager
ARN is returned instead, which lets a caller verify a secret
exists without revealing its value. Ignored when
include_sensitive is false.

post.summary:
ConvertUsersToHuman creates one permanent override rule per affected
provider in that provider's UserDataMappingProfile, forcing the target users
to HUMAN identity type. Input users may span multiple providers; users
belonging to the same provider share a single rule.
To revert a conversion, delete the corresponding rule via the
UserDataMappingProfile rule management API.

ConvertUsersToService creates one permanent override rule per affected
provider in that provider's UserDataMappingProfile, forcing the target users
to SERVICE (NHI) identity type. The per-provider canonical NHI type is
derived server-side. Input users may span multiple providers; users
belonging to the same provider share a single rule.
To revert a conversion, delete the corresponding rule via the
UserDataMappingProfile rule management API.

ROLE_ASSIGNMENT flow but is restricted to providers in the AGENT_PLATFORM
category and to scopes whose backing graph node has agentType != 0
(i.e. only agent resources are reviewed).

Used for UAR campaigns that review agent tool access assignments.

 - OBO_DISCOVERY: Feature flag to enable OAuth token/OBO (On Behalf Of) discovery for Google Workspace and Entra
 - WORKFLOW_INTROSPECTION: Feature flag to enable workflow introspection logging on completion
When enabled, logs inventory statistics summary and raises alerts for failures
 - AGENTS: Feature flag to enable agents dashboard in UI
 - INVENTORY_IRM_BATCH_WRITE: Feature flag to enable batched inventory resource mapping writes.
Rollout can be scoped per handler/path incrementally.
 - RECOMMENDATION_ENGINE_INVENTORY_TRIGGER: Controls whether the inventory workflow chain triggers the recommendation-engine
per-tenant pipeline after query cache completes.
Enabled by default. Disable per tenant to stop rec-engine from being triggered
from inventory without redeploying.
 - ACCOUNT_RECOMENDATIONS_CONFIGURED: Controls whether account-level recommendation tasks are computed for a tenant.
Enabled by default. Disable per tenant to skip account-level fetches
 - USER_ATTRIBUTES: Feature flag to enable user attribute ingestion and storage in PostgreSQL.
When enabled, IDP and HR attributes are persisted per-user and exposed via GraphQL.
 - WEBHOOK_CREATION: Controls whether the webhook creation UI is enabled.
 - CHANNELBOT_V2: When enabled, beacon sends the enriched AccessRequestNotificationPayload
(v2) to the channelbot service instead of the minimal v1 payload.
 - DELTA_APIS_INVENTORY: Controls delta inventory sync (delta API-based incremental sync for
providers that support it, e.g. Entra group memberships).
 - ENTRA_MAILBOX_NHI_DETECTION: Controls mailbox NHI detection in Entra. When enabled, per-user
mailboxSettings API calls identify shared/room/equipment mailboxes as NHIs.
 - STREAMING_INVENTORY_DUMP: STREAMING_INVENTORY_DUMP enables the streaming write architecture for S3 inventory dump.
When active, records flow directly to gzip files as they arrive (no in-memory hierarchy).
Only activate after production metrics show memory pressure or lock contention.
Falls back to improved in-memory S3 dump when not activated.
 - ANDROMEDATESTAPP: This should not be flipped to enabled ever. only for development testing in ci for
andromeda test app.
 - PAGERDUTY: BEGIN-PROVIDERGEN: FeatureType
(auto-generated by tools/providergen from providers/<name>/provider.yaml; do not edit by hand.)
 - WEBEX: END-PROVIDERGEN: FeatureType
 - UNRESTRICTED_APP_UPC_CLEANUP: When enabled, removes stale USER_PROVIDER_CONNECTION edges (and dependent IPB/cache
edges) on unrestricted IDP application providers. Unrestricted apps intentionally
skip UPC computation; this cleans legacy UPC from when the app was restricted or
after isAppRoleAssignmentRequired transitions true -> false.
 - ENTRA_PIM_ELIGIBILITY_INGESTION: When enabled, the Entra ingester collects PIM (Privileged Identity Management)
eligible assignments (directory role + group membership eligibilities) and Kepler
upserts them as managed PolicyEligibilityMappings. Off by default; this side-effects
eligibility config, so enable per tenant after validation.
 - AZURE_PIM_ELIGIBILITY_INGESTION: When enabled, the Azure ingester collects Azure resource PIM (ARM role eligibility
schedule instances) at subscription and resource-group scope and Kepler upserts them as
managed PolicyEligibilityMappings (account-scoped, with a resource-group constraint for
RG-scoped eligibilities). Management-group and below-resource-group scopes are skipped.
Off by default; this side-effects eligibility config, so enable per tenant after validation.
 - INVENTORY_DIGEST_BATCHING: Feature flag to enable batched/deduplicated inventory digest task processing
in kepler (policy, app binding, group membership handlers).
 - GROUP_ATTRIBUTES: Feature flag to enable IDP group attribute ingestion and storage in PostgreSQL.
When enabled, IDP group attributes are persisted per-group and exposed via GraphQL.

JitPolicyTransactionStatusTypeMessageAcc.description:
- CREATED: Initial status of the JitPolicyRequest when it is created by the User.
The JitPolicyTransaction is created right after the JitPolicyRequest is created
with this status (as a transaction). The transaction, is initialized with
status "CREATED".
 - REQUEST_ANALYSIS_IN_PROGRESS: A JitPolicyTransaction is marked SUBMITTED once the JIT Controller reads/registers
the "CREATED" JIT Request.
The JIT Controller must be active to mark the JIT Transaction as SUBMITTED.
As part of the Controller processing, the Request is also sent for Request Analysis
by the Andromeda system.
 - REQUEST_ANALYZED: A JitPolicyTransaction is marked REQUEST_ANALYZED when the JIT Controller gets
a response from the analyzer system.
As part of the Controller processing, the Request is also assigned Reviewers
and Reviewers are notified. The Reviewers can, at this point, view the analyzed
JIT Policy Request, and approval/reject the Request.
 - REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS: JitPolicyRequest is marked REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS once initial set of Reviewers are notified.
Andromeda System then waits for the Approval/Rejection/Timeout of the Reviewers.
The Request stays in this state until all the required Reviewers have responded.
 - APPROVED: JitPolicyRequest is APPROVED once all Reviewers have APPROVED.
 - SCHEDULED_FOR_PROVISIONING: JitPolicyRequest is SCHEDULED_FOR_PROVISIONING for a future time, once it has been APPROVED.
The startTime for the Provisioning is asked as part of the JitPolicyRequest creation.
 - WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_PROVISIONING: The Request is WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_PROVISIONING to be completed, when request profile has
manual provisioning/deprovisioning enabled.
 - PROVISIONING_IN_PROGRESS: Transient
 - PROVISIONED: JIT Session is PROVISIONED and the User can access the resources.
After the Provisioning, the Request is scheduled for Deprovisioning.
 - DEPROVISIONING_IN_PROGRESS: Transient
 - WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_DEPROVISIONING: The Request is WAITING_FOR_MANUAL_DEPROVISIONING to be completed, when request profile has
manual provisioning/deprovisioning enabled.
 - DEPROVISIONED: JIT Session is DEPROVISIONED and the User can no longer access the resources.
After the successful DeProvisioning, the JIT Controller schedules a check to validate whether
the Policy has been Deprovisioned for the User.
 - SESSION_ANALYSIS_PENDING: Once the JIT Controller detects a deprovisioned action, the Session is marked
as pending for analysis by the Session summarizer.
 - CANCELLATION_IN_PROGRESS: Access request status is marked as CANCELLATION_IN_PROGRESS when:
1. The Requester manually ends the session. Here the controller will be cleaning up
  running processes for the request.
 - REJECTED: JitPolicyRequest is REJECTED once a Reviewer rejects the Request.
This is a terminal state.
 - DEPROVISIONING_FAILED: JIT Request is marked as DEPROVISIONING_FAILED when the deprovisioning fails.
Deprovisioning can be retried using the bulk retrigger deprovisioning API.
 - PROVISIONING_FAILED: JIT Request is marked as PROVISIONING_FAILED when the provisioning fails.
Provisioning can be retried using the bulk retrigger provisioning API.
 - FAILED: JIT processing failed during any of the previous steps.
This is a terminal state.
 - TIMED_OUT: Request is Time out when start time passes and review is not approved.
This is a terminal state.
 - CLOSED: Request is closed before PROVISIONED.
This is a terminal state.
 - SKIPPED: When the the access is already provisioned via some other route
we might want to skip provisioning / deprovisioning.
 - COMPLETED: JitPolicyRequest is marked as COMPLETED from either:
1. The Requester manually ending the Session after it is Provisioned, or
2. The Controller archiving it once the Session has been analyzed in the end, or
This is a terminal state.

PromptContextMessagePromptContextType.description:
- UNSPECIFIED: Default fallback. Used when the user's intent is ambiguous, conversational chatter,
or does not cleanly map to specific Andromeda modules.
 - ACCESS_MANAGEMENT: Handles queries related to permissions rightsizing, dynamic least privilege,
and Just-In-Time (JIT) access requests. Route here if the user asks to modify,
grant, revoke, request, or approve permissions, entitlements, or roles for
human users or non-human identities (like API keys, service accounts, or tokens).
 - IDENTITY_GOVERNANCE: Handles queries regarding identity lifecycles, user access reviews (UAR),
compliance frameworks (e.g., PCI DSS, ISO 27001, NY DFS), and identity inventory.
Route here if the user asks about scheduling access reviews, auditing stale accounts,
tracking human/NHI identity sprawl, or pulling compliance posture evidence.
 - SECURITY_INSIGHTS_AND_SUGGESTIONS: Handles queries regarding real-time identity risk scoring, behavioral analysis,
anomaly detection, and operational threat hunting. Route here if the user asks
about identity breaches, suspicious activity logs, privilege escalations,
break-glass accounts missing MFA, or needs remediation suggestions for security gaps.
 - AGENTIC_AI: Handles queries regarding the security, lifecycle, permissions, and behavior
of autonomous AI agents, machine identities, and automated LLM workflow extensions
operating within the cloud or SaaS environment. Route here if the user explicitly
asks about monitoring or securing Agentic AI and machine-era infrastructure.

ServiceIdentitySignificanceTypeMessageSe.description:
- CROSS_ACCOUNT_WITH_CRITICALITY_ESCALATION: Anyone of the owners is a stale owner or deactived owner.
Cross account access with criticality escalation
 - SUPER_ADMIN: Deprecated
 - EKS_CLUSTER_NOT_FOUND: If a service identity has some inconsistency
 - MULTIPLE_NHIS_SHARE_SAME_AWS_ROLE: multiple service identities that were discovered from the same role
 - INACTIVE_30_90_DAYS: last activity seen.
 - NHI_WITH_NO_POLICY_BINDINGS: NHI with no policy bindings
 - OVERPRIVILEGED_ROLE: NHI has over provisioned permissions for this assignment in the context.
 - UNUSED_ROLE: NHI has unused assignments permissions in the context.
 - EXTERNAL_CLIENT: If an NHI is externally used. This will automatically include AWS external NHIs and
any NHI that is local but used by an external client.
 - FEDERATED_IDENTITY: GCP workload identity pool synthetic principal or an NHI impersonated by that principal.
 - CREDENTIAL_WITH_PASSWORD: Credential insights — independently computed buckets describing how an NHI
can authenticate. An NHI may match multiple buckets simultaneously (e.g.
an IAM User with both console password access and an enabled access key
carries both PASSWORD and EXPLICIT_KEY). NO_USABLE_CREDENTIALS is the
negation of the other three: it fires iff the NHI has no password, no
usable explicit key, and no implicit credential mechanism.

Source of truth per bucket:
  PASSWORD     — bool `has_password_credential` set by the ingester on
                 the bound User node (provider-specific signal — e.g.
                 AWS IAM LoginProfile, Okta credentials.password).
  EXPLICIT_KEY — derived in querycache from UserAccessKey rows
                 (`isEnabled = true` AND not past `keyExpiresAt`).
  IMPLICIT_KEY — bool `has_implicit_key_credential` set by the ingester
                 on the bound User node based on the NHI subtype
                 (instance-profile, managed identity, etc.).
  NO_USABLE_CREDENTIALS — pure Cypher negation of the above three.
 - RECENT_FAILED_ACTIONS: Service identity has had at least one error/failed provider action
(error_lookup.is_error = true) within the recent lookback window (30 days).

Detected via /mcpservers row, x-ms-agentic-protocol on the connector
Swagger, or `kind: ModelContextProtocolMetadata` in the action YAML.
 - DATA_CONNECTOR: REST connector — the conventional Power Platform connector shape
(Swagger-described HTTP). Covers BOTH first-party shared_* connectors
(SharePoint, Teams, Salesforce) and tenant-imported custom connectors;
the BUILT_IN vs CUSTOM split lives on ToolProvenanceEnum, not here.

enum — semantically equivalent to "REST connector".

Microsoft/anyone ships A2A on Power Platform; classifier doesn't emit
this yet but the value is here so downstream filters don't need a
schema bump when it lands.

WorkflowLevelMessageWorkflowLevel.title:
- GLOBAL: Global workflows orchestrate across all tenants (no tenant_id, no provider_id)
 - TENANT: Tenant workflows orchestrate providers within a single tenant (has tenant_id, no provider_id)
 - PROVIDER: Provider workflows are specific to one provider (has tenant_id and provider_id)

WorkflowTypeMessageWorkflowType.description:
- INVENTORY_PARENT_WF: Parent workflow type that creates child INVENTORY workflows via ANDROMEDA_WORKFLOW tasks
This type bypasses per-provider blocking for INVENTORY workflows, preventing deadlocks
 - SUGGESTED_OWNERS: Workflow type for resolving suggested owners from TSDB logs
 - DELTASYNC_SYNC: Workflow type for delta sync sync phase (reads DELTA mode resources from IR, publishes to Kepler)
Mutually exclusive with INVENTORY workflows per provider
 - ANALYTICS: Workflow type for analytics runs (behavior models, and future analytics tasks like lsp-eps, Galileo).
Scheduled via knot; runs at GLOBAL level. Managed by AnalyticsController.
 - ON_DEMAND_ANALYSIS: Generic on-demand analysis workflow. Routes to any service implementing ExecutionService.
Use for per-tenant, API-triggered analyses (ariel group anomaly, unused groups, etc.).
Independent concurrency from ANALYTICS — does not block behavior model runs.
 - TEST_CONNECTIVITY: Workflow type for testing provider connectivity
 - GRAPH_SYNC: Workflow type for async graph sync operations in polaris (ToolApplication, AccessPolicy, PolicyBinding).
 - GRAPH_JANITOR: Workflow type for the monthly graph soft-delete janitor. Scheduled via knot;
runs at GLOBAL level as a single Kubernetes Job (GRAPH_JANITOR task, KUBERNETES runtime).

Cooper session, e.g. "sess-01JZ...".

e.g. "github-prod".

applicationName.description:
application_name is the display name of the governed application, e.g.
"GitHub Enterprise".

toolName.description: tool_name is the MCP tool invoked on the application, e.g. "repos_list".

policyId.description:
policy_id is the access policy that authorized or denied the call, e.g.
"policy_abc".

callIndex.description: call_index is the position of this tool call within the session, e.g. 3.

httpStatus.description: http_status is the upstream HTTP status observed by the gateway, e.g. 200.

status.description: status is the normalized gateway decision/runtime result, e.g. ALLOW.

credentialMode.description: credential_mode is the outbound credential mode, e.g. "oauth_obo".

sourceIp.description: source_ip is the client IP observed by the gateway, e.g. "10.1.44.2".

latencyMs.description:
latency_ms is the end-to-end request latency in milliseconds as measured by
Envoy (time to last downstream tx byte), e.g. 142. Nullable: NULL for rows
written before Envoy access logging landed.

modelIntent.description:
model_intent is the agent-declared, free-text purpose for the call, captured
from the injected _andromeda_model_intent argument, e.g. File the bug report
the user asked for in repo acme-widgets. SIGNAL ONLY: recorded for audit and
risk review, never an input to the authorization decision. Empty when the
agent omitted it or the tool predates intent capture. Not low-cardinality:
this is high-cardinality free text.

userIntent.description:
user_intent is the original end-user request that started the session, echoed
by the agent, e.g. Summarize the attached quarterly report PDF. Constant
across a session; recover the session origin with
argMin(user_intent, timestamp) GROUP BY session_id. SIGNAL ONLY: recorded for
audit and risk review, never an input to the authorization decision. Empty
when not captured. Not low-cardinality: high-cardinality free text.

email.description:
Email can either be of a SSO User, or a non-SSO User. The type of
User (SSO/non-SSO) is determined by checking the domain in the Email.
A non-SSO User is logged in via an OTP to the Email.
An SSO User on the other hand is logged in by redirecting it to

email.description:
Email is the email of the User who wishes to access Andromeda resources.
Email is optional in AccessKeyLogin, and required in EmailLogin and SAMLLogin.

code.description:
Code is determined by what authentication flow is being used.
If the Login is initiated via the OTP flow, the code is the OTP sent on mail.
If the Login is initiated via the SAML flow, the code is what the IdP provides
post the redirects.
IF the Login is via the Access key flow, the code is the generated access key.

apiOnDemandAnalysisType.description:
OnDemandAnalysisType identifies which analysis to run via TriggerOnDemandAnalysis.
Add a new value here when a new on-demand analysis is wired up.

 - IDP_GROUP_OUTLIER: Group IDP anomaly detection — runs ariel's GroupMemberAnomalyWorkflow for the given tenant.
 - DORMANT_GROUPS: Dormant groups detection — runs ariel's GroupDormantWorkflow for the given tenant.
 - RISK_RECOMPUTE: Full tenant risk recomputation — runs kuiper's risk trigger (the same
ExecutionService method knot fires after each inventory sync), recomputing
the entire tenant risk pipeline. Heavy; prefer AGENT_RISK_RECOMPUTE for
agent-link-driven refreshes.
 - AGENT_RISK_RECOMPUTE: Scoped agent risk recomputation — runs only the agent-affecting steps
(agent risk + effective risk) rather than the whole tenant pipeline. Fired
when an inventory provider link changes so agent effective risk reflects
the new operator bound without a full tenant recompute.

userIds.description:
Clients can optionally provide user IDs to trigger the policy evaluation for a specific user/s.
If not provided, the engine tries to find the Users based on the provider_id and event_type 
and the last policy run. It will choose those users in the provider for which 
the policy was not yet evaluated before this trigger.
If between the last policy run and the trigger, the engine detected USER_JOIN events, then
the engine will choose those users.
If userIds are provided, then the engine totally relies on the user input provided with the trigger.

workflowDefinitionId.title:
Optional. The workflow definition to instantiate. When supplied, the
definition's Type drives composer selection. Required for workflow types
that rely on the generic composer (ANALYTICS, SUGGESTED_OWNERS,
QUERY_CACHE_TIME_DEPENDENT) because their task templates live in
WorkflowDefinition.task_definitions; for hard-coded composer types
(INVENTORY) this field is purely metadata and may be omitted in favor of
workflow_type.
Example: "8b0c1c8a-3a3a-4a3a-9a3a-1c8a3a3a4a3a"

workflowType.description:
Optional. Workflow type to trigger when workflow_definition_id is omitted,
or as a sanity-check when both are supplied. The server uses this to pick
the composer and, when no workflow_definition_id is supplied, to look up
the canonical WorkflowDefinition for the type (or to synthesize defaults
for types backed by a hard-coded composer).

apiTriggerTenantWorkflowRequest.description:
TriggerTenantWorkflowRequest triggers a tenant-level workflow for the caller's
tenant by composing tasks via the registered or generic composer.

Behavior mirrors the global-schedule path in knot: a synthetic schedule is built
for the caller's tenant with is_global=false, then handed to the appropriate
composer (e.g., InventoryTenantComposer for INVENTORY workflows). The resulting
task definitions are persisted as a single tenant-level workflow with provider
child workflow tasks.

At least one of {workflow_definition_id, workflow_type} must be supplied:
  * workflow_definition_id alone   - load that exact definition; its Type drives
                                     the composer choice.
  * workflow_type alone            - server resolves the canonical
                                     WorkflowDefinition for the type. For types
                                     backed by a hard-coded composer (currently
                                     INVENTORY) the server falls back to default
                                     values when no row exists. For types that
                                     depend on the generic composer (ANALYTICS,
                                     SUGGESTED_OWNERS, QUERY_CACHE_TIME_DEPENDENT)
                                     a row MUST exist because the recipe lives
                                     in WorkflowDefinition.task_definitions.
  * both                           - workflow_definition_id wins; workflow_type
                                     is validated to match WD.Type.

assignReviewersTemplate.description:
AssignReviewersTemplate represents the chain of approvers in the intender order,
with the first set of reviewers assigned from the first index and so on.
It'll allow the reviewer configuration to look something like this:
assign_reviewers_template: [
  {persona: IDENTITY, persona_values: ["user1", "user2", "user3"], required_approvals: 2},
  {persona: GROUP_MEMBER, persona_values: ["group1"], assignable_reviewers: 3, required_approvals: 1},
  {persona: MANAGER, required_approvals: 1},
  {persona: MANAGER, required_approvals: 1},
  {persona: ACCOUNT_OWNER, assignable_reviewers: 2, required_approvals: 1},
]
Manager has a special handling which is when a manager follows a manager, it is
intended to go to the manager of the previous manager.
DEPERECATED.

the number of approvals required from these personas for the AccessRequest to be

configAgentGroupPolicyBinding.description:
AgentGroupPolicyBinding is a join record that binds an AgentAccessPolicy
to an AgentGroup. This is the DISTRIBUTION mechanism — it determines which
policies are candidates for evaluation when an agent in the group makes a
tool call.

Two-phase contract:
  1. DISTRIBUTION (this table): binding makes the policy visible to all
     members of the bound group.
  2. EVALUATION (policy's principal_match): further narrows which agents
     within the group the policy actually fires for.

A policy with no bindings can still target a group directly via
principal_match.kind = GROUP — this is the "standalone policy" path.
When bindings exist, they take precedence over principal_match for
distribution; the policy's principal_match becomes the eval-time filter.

Example: bind the "read-only-github" policy to the "eng-readers" group.

matchNameValue.description:
In case the template variable does not correspond to a valid value in the JIT context,
For instance if JIT is at an Account level but the template provides a resourceGroup variable,
The resourceGroup variable will be replaced with an empty string.

Example usage:
my-prefix-{{accountName}}-{{policyName}}--{{resourceGroupId}}
In this example, if accountName is "exampleAccount", policyName is "examplePolicy", and
resourceGroupId is "rg-12345", the resolved string would be:
my-prefix-exampleAccount-examplePolicy--rg-12345
This is the group that will be used to provision an access request for
Polcy `examplePolicy` at a ResourceGroup `rg-12345``, in Account `exampleAccount`.

This field accepts a templated string format where specific variables will be
substituted with their corresponding values at runtime - while provisioning / deprovisioning.
Supported template variables are:
{{accountId}}, {{accountName}}
{{policyId}}, {{policyName}} and
{{resourceGroupId}}, {{resourceGroupName}}

Enum to specify the type of matching criteria.

 - UNSPECIFIED: Default value indicating no specific criteria set. This will be treated as an error.
 - SUFFIX: Matches if the target ends with the specified value.
 - PREFIX: Matches if the target starts with the specified value.
 - EXACT: Matches if the target is an exact match with the specified value.
 - REGEX: For example, the normal user is kamal.murali@andromedasecurity.com and the privileged user is
“su-kamal.murali@andromedasecurity.com”. In this case after you remove the prefix, the username
is an exact match to the HI username. The normal user is kamal.murali@andromedasecurity.com and
the privileged user is “su-kmurali@andromedasecurity.com” . Now we need to form the privileged
user username using first letter of first name appended with last name with a prefix of “su-”

configPolicyTypeMessagePolicyType.description:
- AWS_PERMISSION_SET: AWS Permission Set in AWS Identity Center
 - AWS_IAM_ROLE: AWS Role in IAM
 - AWS_USER_PERMISSIONS: AWS User-level permission policies
 - AWS_GROUP_PERMISSIONS: AWS Group-level permission policies
 - GCP_ROLE: GCP Role
 - WORKSPACE_ROLE: Workspace role
 - WORKSPACE_OAUTH_OBO_POLICY: Workspace OAuth OBO (On Behalf Of) policy - represents OAuth scopes granted to third-party apps
 - AZURE_ROLE: Azure role
 - ENTRA_OAUTH_OBO_POLICY: Entra OAuth OBO (On Behalf Of) policy - represents OAuth scopes granted to third-party apps
 - AWS_ROOT: AWS Root policy
 - SCIM_PUSH_GROUP_ROLE: these are roles created from the scim push groups that are synced
from the IDP to the provider. (shadow of a push group in app-bound provider)
 - UNIT_POLICY: Unit policy means "has access". This and corresponding binding objects should not be shown in UI.
 - CUSTOM_APP_ROLE: Role in Custom App
 - CUSTOM_APP_USER_ROLE: User role in Custom App. This is used when andromeda creates a user specific role
that cannot be mapped directly to an Application role
 - ENTRA_ROLE: Roles from Entra
 - ENTRA_BUILTIN_ROLE: Entra built-in and custom roles (distinct from generic ENTRA_ROLE)
 - PINGONE_ROLE: Naming kept to avoid migration issue.
 - EKS_ACCESS_POLICY: Roles from EKS
 - ATLAS_DATABASE_CUSTOM_ROLE: Roles from Atlas
 - OKTA_STANDARD_ROLE: Okta roles
 - ELASTIC_ORGANIZATION_ROLE: Roles from Elastic
 - ANDROMEDA_RESOURCE_POLICY: Resource Policies
 - SNOWFLAKE_CUSTOM_ROLE: Roles from Snowflake (built-in = standard roles like ACCOUNTADMIN, custom = everything else)
 - SLACK_WORKSPACE_BUILT_IN_ROLE: Roles from Slack Enterprise
 - RDS_POSTGRESQL_ROLE: RDS Role
 - GITHUB_REPOSITORY_ROLE: Roles from GitHub
 - KEEPER_ROLE: Roles from Keeper
 - GITLAB_BUILTIN_ROLE: Roles from GitLab
 - DATABRICKS_ACCOUNT_ENTITLEMENT_ROLE: Roles from Databricks
3 account level entitlements
 - DATABRICKS_ACCOUNT_WORKSPACE_MGMT_ROLE: 2 workspace managment roles
 - DATABRICKS_WORKSPACE_ENTITLEMENT_ROLE: 4 workspace level entitlements
 - DATABRICKS_WORKSPACE_DASHBOARD_ROLE: workspace resource roles
 - DATABRICKS_METASTORE_GRANT_ROLE: metastore grant roles
 - ATLASSIAN_ROLE: Roles from Atlassian
 - NETAPP_ROLE: Roles from NetApp
 - ZOOM_BUILTIN_ROLE: Roles from Zoom
 - JIRA_GLOBAL_PERMISSION: Roles from Jira
 - GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_SYSTEM_ROLE: google workspace role
 - GCP_SYSTEM_ROLE: Gcp role
 - ACTIVE_DIRECTORY_ROLE: Roles from Active Directory
 - AZURE_BUILTIN_ROLE: Azure built-in and custom roles (distinct from generic AZURE_ROLE)
 - WINDOWS_FILE_SERVER_ROLE: Roles from Windows File Server
 - COPILOT_STUDIO_ROLE: Copilot Studio agent roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer)
 - TOOL_CLIENT: Agent tool client — represents a connection reference binding between
an agent instance and an external tool/connector
 - AZURE_FOUNDRY_ROLE: Azure-side role definition copied into the Foundry provider, filtered by
hasAgentPermissions = true. Mirrors KUBERNETES_AZURE_ROLE for AKS but
scoped to the Azure Foundry provider's view (no cross-provider graph
edges — joined by externalId at query time).
 - GRAFANA_ROLE: Grafana org basic role (Viewer/Editor/Admin) and folder ACL permission
(View/Edit/FolderAdmin) — shared PolicyType for all Grafana scopes.
 - TOOL_APPLICATION_ACCESS_POLICY: Policy that lives entirely inside the Andromeda agent gateway:
declares which tool actions on which ToolApplication a principal
can perform. Sourced from apiserver `tool_application_access_policies`
(not from any external provider). Projected into the graph as a
Policy node scoped under the ToolApplication.
 - CURSOR_DESKTOP_ROLE: Cooper desktop agent platform roles (Owner)
 - CLAUDE_PLATFORM_ORG_ROLE: Claude Platform organization and workspace built-in member roles.
 - CLOUDFLARE_MEMBER_PG: Cloudflare member permission group — assignable to humans on an
account. Atomic role (permission == PG name); never modeled via
the legacy resource:verb grid (the grid is lossy; see role-scope.md).
 - CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN_PG: Cloudflare token-plane PG registry, shared by account- and user-owned
tokens (they share UUIDs). Distinct from the member PG catalog.
 - RETOOL_BUILTIN_ROLE: Retool organisation roles (provider-scoped). Builtin = isDefaultRole,
custom = everything else. Permissions sourced from organizationScopes.
 - RETOOL_OBJECT_ACCESS_ROLE: Retool per-object access policy. One Policy per app/folder/resource/
workflow whose document is the native access list (use/edit/own); the
per-principal level is read from the document, not the policy.

isPrivilegedUser.description:
Mark the user as privileged user which matched the pattern.

certificateAuth.description:
Self-service: customer pastes identity file content from `tctl auth sign`.

The UI should display credential_expires_at and warn before expiry.

botAuth.description:
Managed deployment: requires Andromeda ops to deploy a tbot sidecar.
NOT available for self-service provider configuration.
tbot runs alongside the ingester, authenticates with the join token,
and writes renewable identity files to identity_output_path.

configTeleportAuthMode.description:
- TELEPORT_AUTHMODE_CERTIFICATE: Self-service: customer pastes identity file PEM content.
Credentials are static and expire; the UI warns before expiry.
Generated via: tctl auth sign --user=<user> --format=file --ttl=8760h

Requires Andromeda ops to deploy a tbot sidecar alongside the ingester.
tbot handles automatic certificate renewal using the join token.

identityFile.description:
Identity file content (PEM certificate + private key). Generate via:

Then paste the file content here.
Example: -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...

credentialExpiresAt.description:

The UI uses this to show remaining validity and warn before expiry.

findings.title:

description and schema. Empty = scan found nothing. Advisory only.

location.title:

JSON inside ToolApplicationDiscoveredTool.findings — it is not its own table.

dataplaneAgentConnectionAssignment.description:
AgentConnectionAssignment is one resolved (agent, app) → connection row from
the graph. agent_external_id is the gateway-facing id (matches the
x-mcp-agent-id the broker presents); application_id is the ToolApplication id;
connection carries the decrypted credential for cooper to persist to ASM.

agentExternalId.description:
Gateway-facing agent id. Matches x-mcp-agent-id stamped by the
role-mapper (the registered agent's oauth_client_id).

sponsorEmail.description:
Sponsor's email as recorded at registration. The DP normalizes this to
the same key space as x-mcp-user-id (email local-part) when compiling
the OPA document.

dataplaneAgentSponsor.description:
AgentSponsor maps a registered agent's gateway external id (the OAuth
client id the agent authenticates with) to its sponsor's email. Only
ACTIVE agents with both facets present are returned; the DP reconciles
by absence, so a disabled or deleted agent drops out of the map on the
next sync.

agentInvocations.description:
Non-interactive agents only; the broker joins this against per-app,
per-invocation-type override rows.

dataplaneOnboardedSubjectAttributes.description:
OnboardedSubjectAttributes is one subject's attribute snapshot for the data
plane. subject_email is the gateway lookup key (the DP keys subject_attrs by
the email local-part = x-mcp-user-id). Enum-valued attributes are sent as
their canonical name (HUMAN/SERVICE, LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) so they line up with
the values policy authors pick; an unspecified enum is sent empty. attributes
carries any extra IdP/HR facets as a flat string bag.

status.description:
Flattened from ToolApplicationStatus. Zero values mean "no status
row yet" / "never probed". PROBE_FAILED on status + last_probe_error
together convey the previous failure detail without a separate enum.

updatedAt.description:
App's own updated_at. Informational only — use effective_updated_at
below for cursor advancement.

effectiveUpdatedAt.description:
GREATEST watermark (see service doc). DP feeds this back as
updated_since on the next call.

inventoryProviderLink.description:
Optional inventory provider link for resource-scoped gateway authz.
CASE uses provider_type to configure the mcp-dispatcher WASM extractor.

captureIntent.description:
When true, CASE injects the required intent field into this application's
served tool input schemas (audit/risk signal only). Opt-in per application.

dataplaneOnboardedToolApplication.description:
OnboardedToolApplication is the DP projection of an onboarded
ToolApplication. Status fields are flattened in; embedded leaf
value types (AppMcpServerConfig, AppAuthProfile, AppOwnerDetails)
are reused from configpb because they are not table-backed.

auth_profile is returned decrypted — treat as carrying secrets.

actions.description:
Reused from configpb because it's a JSONB-embedded value type,
not a table-backed row.

resourceConditions.description:
Policy-level resource scoping predicates evaluated at tools/call time
against x-cooper-res-<attribute> headers stamped by the dispatcher.
Subject attribute predicates (subject.*) also ride this field; the DP
evaluates them against the calling subject's synced subject_attrs.

agentExternalId.description:
─── Principal slot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
Gateway external IDs resolved by polaris at binding write time. These
match the headers stamped by the datapath role-mapper (x-mcp-agent-id /
x-ms-entra-agent-id and x-mcp-user-id). Internal Andromeda UUIDs are
not exposed on this RPC.

sponsoredBySubject.description:
Sponsored-agents runtime principal: the runtime axis matches any
registered agent whose sponsor is the user matched on the subject axis.
When set, agent_external_id and agent_group_id are empty; the DP keys
the tuple under the synthetic sponsored agent key instead of a concrete
or group key.

subjectConditions.description:
Subject (delegator identity) ABAC conditions authored on the binding, e.g.
subject.department IN [eng]. The DP merges these with the bound policy's
resource_conditions and evaluates the union against the synced subject_attrs
snapshot at tools/call time. Only subject.* attributes appear here.

dataplaneOnboardedToolApplicationAccessP.description:
OnboardedToolApplicationAccessPolicyBinding is the DP projection of an
apiserver ToolApplicationAccessPolicyBinding row. The gateway only
needs the principal slot, the anchor application, the policy id (to
join against the locally cached allowed-tools/actions), and the
effect + conditions to enforce at call time.

`application_id` is the binding's scope anchor. In v0 it always equals
the parent policy's application_id; the field is denormalized onto
the binding row in apiserver and surfaced here so the DP can route a
binding to its application cache without an extra lookup.

Principal slot semantics match the source row: at least one of the
four id fields is set. For concrete (agent, user) bindings the
*_external_id fields carry gateway subject ids; group slots are
reserved for future use.

dataplaneOnboardedToolApplicationTool.description:
OnboardedToolApplicationTool is the DP projection of a
ToolApplicationAllowedTool. Allowlist rows are sticky once persisted —
the DP just consumes whatever risk/access is currently stored without
needing to know whether it came from the classifier or an admin edit.

requestId.description:
Id of the access-request row polaris created. Empty when success
is false.

success.description:
True iff polaris accepted the request and persisted a row. On
false, see error_message for the reason (e.g. unknown application,
tool not in allowlist, principal lookup failed).

errorMessage.description: Human-readable error detail. Empty on success.

dataplaneResolvedConnection.description:
ResolvedConnection is the datapath projection of a ToolApplicationConnection
row with decrypted auth_profile. Carried inside AgentConnectionAssignment so
cooper can persist the connection's secret to ASM.

dataplaneToolApplicationResourceFacet.description:
ToolApplicationResourceFacet is one resource's tag labels for gateway lookup.
resource_path matches the x-cooper-res-resource_path header stamped by the
dispatcher; tag_values are the labels policy authors pick (e.g. env:prod).

acceptedCount.description: accepted_count is the number of rows accepted by Polaris for persistence.

usagePattern.title: usage_pattern is the detected usage pattern type (RARELY_USED, CYCLICAL, FREQUENT_GAPS, CONSTANTLY_USED, SPORADIC, INSUFFICIENT_DATA)

galileoUsagePatternMetadata.title: UsagePatternMetadata contains pattern analysis metadata for usage patterns

name.description:
The server-assigned name, which is only unique within the same service that
originally returns it. If you use the default HTTP mapping, the
`name` should be a resource name ending with `operations/{unique_id}`.

metadata.description:
Service-specific metadata associated with the operation.  It typically
contains progress information and common metadata such as create time.
Some services might not provide such metadata.  Any method that returns a
long-running operation should document the metadata type, if any.

done.description:
If the value is `false`, it means the operation is still in progress.
If `true`, the operation is completed, and either `error` or `response` is
available.

error.description: The error result of the operation in case of failure or cancellation.

response.description:
The normal response of the operation in case of success.  If the original
method returns no data on success, such as `Delete`, the response is
`google.protobuf.Empty`.  If the original method is standard
`Get`/`Create`/`Update`, the response should be the resource.  For other
methods, the response should have the type `XxxResponse`, where `Xxx`
is the original method name.  For example, if the original method name
is `TakeSnapshot()`, the inferred response type is
`TakeSnapshotResponse`.

googlelongrunningOperation.description:
This resource represents a long-running operation that is the result of a
network API call.

code.description:
The status code, which should be an enum value of
[google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description:
A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any
user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the
[google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized
by the client.

details.description:
A list of messages that carry the error details.  There is a common set of
message types for APIs to use.

googlerpcStatus.description:
The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for
different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is
used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains
three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details.

You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the
[API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

providerId.description:

GetAccessKeysSummary callsite so that resolver-backed sub-fields
(e.g. keys_metadata_bucket_summary) can re-derive the same scope

keysMetadataBucketSummary.description:
Per-key-dimension bucket summary. Today bucketizes "days until
expiry" across active (enabled + non-expired + has expiry) keys.

Accepts an optional BucketConfig argument; when omitted the resolver
defaults to ExplicitBucketConfig{ bounds: [14, 30, 90] } so the
response naturally maps to the spec buckets:
  [0, 14) days   -> "Less than 14 days"
  [14, 30) days  -> "14d - 30d"
  [30, 90) days  -> "30d - 90d"
  90+ days       -> "90d+"

total_keys on the summary equals "Active Keys with expiration"
(the sum of all four buckets).

Also accepts an optional KeysSummaryCountFilters argument so callers
can shape the bucketed key pool. Callers should pass the same filters
they passed to AccessKeysSummary so that the eager counts on the
parent and the buckets describe the same key pool. When omitted the
bucket summary is computed against the unfiltered scope.

graphBucketOptions.description:
`BucketOptions` describes the bucket boundaries used to create a histogram
for the distribution. The buckets can be in a linear sequence, an
exponential sequence, or each bucket can be specified explicitly.
`BucketOptions` does not include the number of values in each bucket.

A bucket has an inclusive lower bound and exclusive upper bound for the
values that are counted for that bucket. The upper bound of a bucket must
be strictly greater than the lower bound. The sequence of N buckets for a
distribution consists of an underflow bucket (number 0), zero or more
finite buckets (number 1 through N - 2) and an overflow bucket (number N -
1). The buckets are contiguous: the lower bound of bucket i (i > 0) is the
same as the upper bound of bucket i - 1. The buckets span the whole range
of finite values: lower bound of the underflow bucket is -infinity and the
upper bound of the overflow bucket is +infinity. The finite buckets are
so-called because both bounds are finite.

[More complex case] user-A has PSet-1 in account-A and Pset-2 in account-B.

But also has lateral access from account-A (role-abe in account-B has trust to PSet-A in account-A).
Do we need to reflect both cases of "Self" and cross? It could have cross from multiple accounts.
Do we need to reflect it? IdentityOriginAccountId should reflect [account-A, account-B]
No issue with Service-Role is it can only be in one account.
Challenges with IAM user (which we classify as human and merge if username is same in multiple accounts).
iam-user foo exists in a-A + a-B + a-Z. In account C there are two roles - r-1 with trust to a-A/foo and r-2 with trust to a-B/foo.
In addition, (no trust for a-Z/foo for any role) in Account-C's human
list we must list foo as cross and origin-account needs to be repeated and list a-A, a-B

count.description:
The range of the population values.
The number of values in the population. Must be non-negative. This value
must equal the sum of the values in `bucket_counts` if a histogram is
provided.

bucketOptions.description:
Defines the histogram bucket boundaries. If the distribution does not
contain a histogram, then omit this field.

bucketCounts.description:
The number of values in each bucket of the histogram, as described in
`bucket_options`. If the distribution does not have a histogram, then omit
this field. If there is a histogram, then the sum of the values in
`bucket_counts` must equal the value in the `count` field of the
distribution.

If present, `bucket_counts` should contain N values, where N is the number
of buckets specified in `bucket_options`. If you supply fewer than N
values, the remaining values are assumed to be 0.

The order of the values in `bucket_counts` follows the bucket numbering
schemes described for the three bucket types. The first value must be the
count for the underflow bucket (number 0). The next N-2 values are the
counts for the finite buckets (number 1 through N-2). The N'th value in
`bucket_counts` is the count for the overflow bucket (number N-1).

bounds.description: The values must be monotonically increasing.

graphExplicit.description:
Specifies a set of buckets with arbitrary widths.

There are `size(bounds) + 1` (= N) buckets. Bucket `i` has the following
boundaries:

   Upper bound (0 <= i < N-1):     bounds[i]
   Lower bound (1 <= i < N);       bounds[i - 1]

The `bounds` field must contain at least one element. If `bounds` has
only one element, then there are no finite buckets, and that single
element is the common boundary of the overflow and underflow buckets.

graphExponential.description:
Specifies an exponential sequence of buckets that have a width that is
proportional to the value of the lower bound. Each bucket represents a
constant relative uncertainty on a specific value in the bucket.

There are `num_finite_buckets + 2` (= N) buckets. Bucket `i` has the
following boundaries:

   Upper bound (0 <= i < N-1):     scale * (growth_factor ^ i).

   Lower bound (1 <= i < N):       scale * (growth_factor ^ (i - 1)).

graphLinear.description:
Specifies a linear sequence of buckets that all have the same width
(except overflow and underflow). Each bucket represents a constant
absolute uncertainty on the specific value in the bucket.

There are `num_finite_buckets + 2` (= N) buckets. Bucket `i` has the
following boundaries:

   Upper bound (0 <= i < N-1):     offset + (width * i).

   Lower bound (1 <= i < N):       offset + (width * (i - 1)).

Filter for resources (folders) to be included in the access review.
Only allowed with the entitlement type of RESOURCE_ACCESS

resourcesTagMatch.description:
Filter all resources that match the tag criteria. Cannot be combined with resource_match.
Only allowed with the entitlement type of RESOURCE_ACCESS.

eligibilityStatusMatch.description: Filter eligibilities by their status for ELIGIBILITY campaigns.

identitySignificanceMatch.description:
Filter identities by identity significance. IN includes identities with at least one
listed significance; NOT_IN excludes identities with any listed significance. Exclude
takes precedence when combined with include filters on the same identity.

userBelongsToGroupMatch.description:
Filter users by group membership. Restricts the campaign to users who belong to specified groups.
Differs from group_match (field 8) which filters groups themselves or identity-group relationships.
Example: {"match_criteria": "IN", "group_ids": ["eng-team-uuid", "admin-group-uuid"]} includes users in these groups.

userSignificanceMatch.description:
Filter users by user-level significance. IN includes users with at least one listed significance;
NOT_IN excludes users with any listed significance. Complements identity_significance_match (field 18) 
which operates on identity-level significance aggregation.
Example: {"match_criteria": "NOT_IN", "values": ["ADMIN_PRIVILEGES", "SUPER_ADMIN"]} excludes high-privilege users.

identityBelongsToGroupMatch.description: Example: {"match_criteria": "IN", "group_ids": ["group-123"]} includes identities that belong to this group.

owners.title:
Resource-level owners discovered from the source provider (e.g. M365 group
owners for a Microsoft Teams team). Mirrored from
inventorymodel.Account.owners by Kepler's AccountConfigCreateTask (upsert)
and read by AssetResolutionTask to resolve owner external IDs into identity
bindings for the asset/UAR pipeline. Mirrors the pattern used by
Group.owners and AndromedaUser.owners. Example:
  owners: [{ id: "<entra_user_id>", external_owner_type: RESOURCE_TYPE_AZURE_ENTRA_USER }]

modelsconfigAccount.description:
It is a Andromeda Account resource that holds common attributes that are configurations and settings
related to Andromeda features related to a provider account. All the learnt information about the
provider cloud would be in a referenced provider specific resource Eg. AWSAccount, GCPAccount etc.

referencedPolicyIds.description: IDs of existing ToolApplicationAccessPolicy rows in this bundle.

policies.description:
Input-only on create/update: new access policies to create and attach.
Replaces the old inline_rules JSONB. Not stored on the bundle row; created
policy IDs are merged into referenced_policy_ids.

id.title: System-generated UUID. Example: "agrp-a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"

name.title:
Human-readable group name, unique within a tenant.
Example: "eng-readers"

description.title:
One-line description of the group's purpose.
Example: "Read-only access to engineering tools for all dev agents."

attributes.title:
Free-form key-value attributes consumed by the policy evaluator for
attribute-based matching (e.g. tier=PRODUCTION, dept=finance).
Stored as JSONB.
Example: {"tier": "PRODUCTION", "dept": "engineering"}

updatedAt.title: Note: created_at is auto-generated by the model generator and should not be defined here

modelsconfigAgentGroup.description:
AgentGroup is a named collection of AI agents that share a common access
boundary. Access policy bundles and individual access policies are bound to
groups — the gateway evaluates every member agent against those bindings
at tool-call time.

Example: "eng-readers" — a group whose members can read GitHub repos
and list ServiceNow incidents.

entitlementType.description:
This represents the type of access review entitlements being
reviewed.

campaignOwnerTemplates.description:
CampaignOwnersTemplates are used to assign owners to the campaign instance.
We try finding every identity that matches the ORed aggregate of the
CampaignOwnersTemplates and assign them the owner role.
Therefore the reviewers can be a union of Identity1, Identity2, accountAdmin and providerOwner.

reviewerAssignmentScheme.description:
Repeated list of reviewer assignment schemes.
Have more than one item in the scheme to support levelled access reviews to be performed
in the campaign. Levelled reviews can be a max of 2 levels.

fallbackReviewerId.description:
Use this reviewer if its set, and user under review is same as 1st level reviewer selected
if nil, no self check, and fallback will be to campaign owner if no valid reviewer ids available
Deprecated: Use the levelled fallback reviewer.

scheduleConfig.description: Campaign Schedule Config is used to schedule the campaign to run at a specific time with a specific frequency.

ownerIds.title:
list of owner ids that this template is associated with, this only work with an identity template
for other templates this needs to be changed

disableSelfReview.title: if set, reviewer will be set to one of manager/fallbackreview/owner if user under review is same as reviewer

restrictReassignmentToOwners.description:
If true, only campaign owners can reassign access reviews to different reviewers.
Reviewers will not be able to reassign reviews assigned to them.

explorerViewConfiguration.description:
Snapshot of the ExplorerView payload sent with POST /explorerviews (CreateExplorerViewRequest.explorerview).
Used for explorer-view remediation campaigns to persist filters, scope, category, notification_policy, etc.

smtpIntegrationId.description:
smtp_integration_id optionally references an Integration of category SMTP
(e.g. Microsoft Exchange) used to deliver review notification emails for
campaigns instantiated from this template. When unset, Andromeda SMTP will be used.

excludeSyncedGroups.title:
If true, for USER_GROUP_ASSIGNMENT campaigns, exclude groups that were synced
into the selected provider from another provider (any incoming GROUP_SYNC_BINDING).
Example: true

accessBundleId.title: Target Access Bundle ID (existence validated at creation)

overrideProfileId.title: Optional: override profile for attribute customization

justification.title: Auto-generated justification text (e.g., "Auto-granted via JML policy")

modelsconfigCreateStandingAssignmentUsin.title:
CreateStandingAssignmentUsingAccessBundleAction grants a standing assignment via an Access Bundle
Including group-membership
Idempotent: skips if user already has access to the bundle

type.title: Type of the explorer view like system, custom

category.title: Category of the explorer view like human, group, resource, nhis, role

ownerId.title: owner of the explorer view. It is possible that it is shared by multiple identities

gqlFiltersJson.title: This is the json version of the gql filters

scopeId.title: Scope ID for filtering explorer views by scope

scopeType.title: Type of scope (PROVIDER, FOLDER, ACCOUNT, RESOURCE_GROUP, etc.)

isCached.description:
When true, this view's results are pre-computed and served from a tachyon dynamic cached set.
Defaults to true for all newly created CUSTOM views.

cacheStatus.description:
Status of the tachyon cache backing this view. OUTPUT_ONLY — set by the server after
RegisterDynamicQuery succeeds or fails.

lastRefreshedAt.description: When the tachyon cache was last successfully refreshed. OUTPUT_ONLY.

remediationCampaignId.title: remediation campaign id for this explorer view

insightTags.title:
Classification tags for explorer view insights (INSIGHT, COMPLIANCE, SECURITY).
Example: ["INSIGHT", "COMPLIANCE"]

modelsconfigExplorerView.description:
Explorer can be of multiple types
Humans, Groups, Resources, NHIs, Roles etc.
For each explorer view there can be multiple filters.

id.title: andromeda uuid

name.title: name of the Access Request Template

description.title: description of the access request template

ownerId.description: This is used for filtering the access request templates by the owner.

eligibilityId.title:
Eligibility ID mapped to the access request from where the favorite was created.
TODO: make this required when JIT team adds eligibility_id to the access requests

accessRequestType.title: access request type whether JIT or Standing

tags.description:
Tags are keywords that store information like JIRA IDs,
github issues. A maximum of 5 keywords are supported.

accountId.description: This is optional because of the folder based JIT.

accessRequestDuration.description:
Duration of the requested JIT Session in seconds. This must be a valid duration window
as defined by the JIT Profile settings based on the eligibility_id.

accessRequestDescription.description: Short reason/description for creating the JitPolicyRequest.

explorerViewIds.title:
Max 20
uuids of the new explorer views

modelsconfigInsightThresholds.description:
InsightThresholds holds configurable thresholds for count-based significances.
A value of 0 (proto3 default) means "not configured at this scope — fall back
to the next-broader scope". If every scope resolves to 0 the significance is
disabled for that run.

category.description: The high-level category of this Integration (e.g. ITSM). Immutable after creation.

type.description: The specific integration tool (e.g. ATLASSIAN_JIRA). Immutable after creation.

name.title: Human-readable policy name (e.g., "Onboarding Policy for Engineering")

trigger.title:
When this policy activates (MANUAL, PROVIDER_EVENT)
These triggers are ORed together

ruleReferences.title: References to JmlRule IDs belonging to this policy

modelsconfigJmlPolicy.description:
JmlPolicy is the top-level entity that defines when JML automation should trigger.
Acts as a container for related JML rules.

name.title: Human-readable rule name (e.g., "Deactivate contractors", "Add to Engineering group")

conditions.title:
Conditions for matching (outer OR, inner AND logic)
Example: [[cond1, cond2], [cond3]] = (cond1 AND cond2) OR cond3
Empty conditions = rule always matches

actions.title: Actions to execute when conditions match (executed in order)

modelsconfigJmlRule.description:
JmlRule defines match conditions and actions to execute.
Rules are associated with policies through JmlPolicy.rule_references.

triggerTypes.title: When this policy activates: MANUAL or PROVIDER_EVENT

providerId.title:
For PROVIDER_EVENT: which provider IDs trigger this policy
Uses user changes in this provider as JML trigger

eventTypes.title: Which lifecycle events activate this policy: JOIN (P1), MOVE (P2), LEAVE (P3)

modelsconfigJmlTrigger.title: JmlTrigger defines when a policy should be evaluated

providerId.description: ProviderId refers to the Provider that the Policy is scoped to.

providerPolicyReference.description: In case of AWS, provider_policy_reference is pset or policy arn.

isLsp.title: is_lsp = true for computed LSP as well as implemented LSP

discoveredTags.description: discovered_tags are the tags that are discovered for the policy.

accountId.description:
AccountId is only set when the Policy is created at the Account level.
If the policy is fetched from a management account/identity center, the Policy
is scoped at the Provider level only, and the AccountId remains empty.

modelsconfigPolicy.description:
Policy in Andromeda represents a set of actions that can be performed on an Account resource.
The Policy can be bound to a User in an Account, which can give the User relevant permissions to
perform the Actions on the Account resource.
These policies are fetched from the Provider, and are stored in Andromeda.
This is currently an immutable object.

name.description:
Name of the eligibility mapping. This is used for display purposes.
It will also be the name of the ResourceSet role Type
That is generated from the eligibility mapping.

accountId.description:
This is optional, and will be filled up if the eligibility is created at 
at an account level. This should be deprecated in favor of scope_id 
(to be introduced later). Right now we support eligibility creation at only
to levels - Provider and Account.
This accountId is where the eligibility belongs, and not the scope where the eligibility is effective.
The eligibility is effective at the eligibility_scope level.

policyId.description:
PolicyId is the id of the policy that is being mapped to the eligibility. It is blank
for provider assignments.
In case of application assignments with push groups, the policy id will be
the id of the shadow policy. Note that the Admins will see these shadow policies
in assignablePolicies list while creating the eligibility.

eligibilityConstraint.title:
Eligibility constrain is used to define scopes under eligibility scope,
where the eligibility applies

provisioningGroupConfiguration.description: The group is picked up from the per role, account Provisioning Group.

profileSelectionConditions.description:
Optional conditional rules for selecting an access request profile.
Example: target_group_before_go_live_profile with access_request_profile_id set to a profile UUID.

roleEligibilityData.title: New Role Eligibility Data when the eligibility_type is ROLE_ELIGIBILITY

eligibleUserIds.title: User IDs who are eligible for the access defined

eligibleGroupIds.title: Groups members are eligible for the access defined

eligibilityScope.description:
ScopeId is the id of the scope where the access will be requested from.
It is the target scope for the eligibility.
For org scoped eligibility, this will be the Provider Id. This means that the
access will be requested for the Org/Provider level. Further constraints could be applied
to the scope via eligibility constraints.
For account scoped eligibility, this will be the Account Id. This means that the
access will be requested for the Account level. 
The scope mentioned here determines the principals, policies, resources that go in the eligibility and are assignable.

accessGroupMatch.title:
Only allowed when the eligibility_type == GROUP_ELIGIBILITY.
Specifies eligibility for a set of groups

provisionViaNhi.title:
Optional. When true, an eligible user self-services a time-bound managed NHI
(a dedicated provider service account) instead of a direct role assignment. This is the
only NHI input the UI sends; the backend derives the provisioning strategy (Grafana ->
dedicated NHI + single time-bound access key) from the provider type at provision time,
and the granted folders/role come from this eligibility's resource-set data.
Example: true

defaultMode.description:
Default Andromeda mode for all the accounts within a provider.
DEPRECATED.

acccountExclusionRules.description:
AccountExclusionRule defines the rule to exclude accounts from the provider.
If the account matches any of the rules, it will be excluded from the discovery.

idpProviderId.description:
This an Optional field indicating the IDP provider where this provider is setup as
an Application. It will not be set for any IDP providers.
Each provider then determines how to use this connection Eg.
In case of IAM SSO all users come from this IDP and it will be a mandatory
configuration. In case of AWS with IDC it is a no-op
In case of Azure the users actually come from the Entra IDP.
When this configuration is set, in the GQL IdpApplicationData will be set.
This field should be set once and immutable as it would create a lot of issues
for the idp applications.

ownerIds.title:
IdentityIds are the Andromeda UUIDs of the identity objects.
@soorajtom - add refrential integrity constraint

priority.description:
Priority of the provider tier. Lower value means higher priority.
1 is the highest priority. 0 is undefined.

modelsconfigProviderType.description:
- PROVIDER_TYPE_IDP_APPLICATION: TODO(P0) AS-3963
All the providers created from the IDP like okta will have
category as IDP_APPLICATION
 - PROVIDER_TYPE_HRIS: generic hris integration

(auto-generated by tools/providergen from providers/<name>/provider.yaml; do not edit by hand.)

Andromeda UUIDs of the roles
List of roles that are related to the service type allowed in the
access request. The payload accepts external role ids instead of role ids
to support policies that are not inventoried as first class Andromeda Roles
in the system and that do not have a Andromeda Policy/Role UUID.

Note: these name need to be in the same order of the

RunJmlRulesAction executes other JML rules (enables composition)
